numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Masked array division (X/2.0) raises a FloatingPointError from an internal multiplication underflow when np.seterr(under='raise') (or np.errstate(under='raise')) is active, because the mask calculation in __call__ only suppresses 'invalid' errors via np.errstate(invalid='ignore').
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The division should complete without raising an underflow FPE; the mask calculation should ignore all floating-point errors (np.errstate(all='ignore')), so X2 equals x/2 elementwise.
trigger_conditions: dividing a numpy masked array (np.ma.array) by a scalar such as 2.0

input_output_examples.input: x = np.arange(0, 3, 0.1); X = np.ma.array(x); with np.errstate(under='raise'): X2 = X/2.0
input_output_examples.buggy_output: underflow FloatingPointError raised inside masked division (plain x/2.0 works)
input_output_examples.expected_output: X2 computed without error and np.testing.assert_array_equal(X2, x/2) holds

category_specific_evidence: Bug #25810: masked array division broken with np.seterr(under='raise'), caused by an internal multiplication underflow in the mask calculation
The fix changes np.errstate(invalid='ignore') to np.errstate(all='ignore') in the domain-mask __call__ computing umath.absolute(a) * self.tolerance >= umath.absolute(b)
The special-value condition is floating-point underflow (FP exception 'under'); the fix suppresses all FP exceptions in the mask calculation rather than only invalid
New test test_masked_array_underflow sets np.errstate(under='raise'), computes X = np.ma.array(np.arange(0, 3, 0.1)), divides by 2.0 and asserts equality with x/2 via np.testing.assert_array_equal
Passages do not mention NaN, +/-inf, signed zero or subnormal inputs, and do not state where they enter; the only handling stated is that the mask computation should ignore FP exceptions
The earlier draft assertion X2.all() == X.all()/2.0 was flagged in review as meaningless; the final test compares arrays directly
The PR date field is empty and the passages do not state the dtype; the tolerance line in the diff context is np.finfo(float).tiny, which is not stated as the test tolerance
reproduction_risks: Reproduction must enable underflow raising (np.errstate(under='raise')) and divide a masked array by 2.0 to trigger the multiply underflow
dtype is not stated in the passages (the diff only uses np.finfo(float), which is float64 by default but the passages do not say the defect is dtype-specific); leave dtype null
Precision and magnitude regime are not stated; the input range 0 to 3 step 0.1 is the only magnitude information
Test tolerance is not stated; assert_array_equal implies exact equality, but no tolerance value appears in the passages
Earlier test version had a faulty assertion (X2.all() == X.all()/2.0); use the final array comparison instead
